Git Model Strategy

Objective and responsibility

The edition preserves a common scientific basis for TEI. Lukas and Nora also work on independent research questions. Miriam Falk is responsible for the official approval; the technology supports modeling, integration and operation.

Setting up and running

The Editionsrepo is located on the institutional GitLab. Two designated persons can arrange administration and restoration. The team starts with a small collection. New employees receive technical introduction, manual and technical exercise with oXygen and the set-up Git client. A correction is compared, backed up, transferred and examined professionally. Conflicts are solved with support, not by keeping a flat file page.

Data and order

Editing units follow stable source references. File names and identifiers do not depend solely on revisable dates. The Editionsrepo contains significant TEI, model rules, documentation and checks. Front end code is separate. Defined exports and proof of origin are secured in the import archive; large image stocks remain in the agreed image infrastructure.

Takeover from Transkribus

The pilot compares PAGE XML with versioned transformation and direct TEI export. After a verified basic transcription, documented export and import, the unit is further processed in the edition repo. Later corrections are carried out specifically. The completion of the regular transcription phase follows an inventory, not only a calendar date.

Research and approval

Limited proposals for changes can be examined in a short branch. Permanently alternative reconstructions receive their own referenced research collections; additional character relations are annotated separately. Starting release, identifiers and later acquisitions remain documented. Private dissertation parts receive matching separate accesses. Sectors do not replace this separation.

Publication

The TEI data, which is scientifically responsible, form the core of our digital edition. The technical frontend provides an interface for the development of the digital edition. Through this interface readers use the comparison and image functions; the same basis can feed further surfaces, print and research. Data sharing and front-end delivery are planned separately and referenced to each other.

approvals combines data, schema and front end status with the required image references. Automatic checks and technical acceptance complement each other. The publisher receives named delivery stands and reports back technical typesetting corrections. The editorial team takes over this control in TEI. One day marks the version; release description and independent archive package complete the marking. Book, data and web offer indicate their actual version relationships.

Further work

The project reviews authorized research holdings and ongoing accesses prior to posting. Separate tasks and available capacities are agreed for post-editing, administration, image operation, frontend and archive. Project and publisher agree in advance on a simple read view and a designated TEI download as a substitute if the edition front end is available later. Scope, data status, care and responsibilities must be recorded. This access does not replace all genetic comparison and image functions. New roles or facilities trigger a new access and agreement check. A recovery and transfer test checks the documentation.

Plan and expected course

The application starts the completion of book, edition frontend and dissertations at the end of the project. The dissertations will last longer even if optimistic estimates are made. Positions and full infrastructure end at the end. The sentence funds are secured; post-editing, continued research access and technical support must be agreed separately. For a delayed front-end start, the agreed replacement route is prepared.

Publish early and concerted

The front end is developed early iteratively and tested with an agreed public function. index, picture view and a search in the released inventory can be used before the complete edition. Chapters and editing stages are supplemented as designated partial releases. Text releases and own research results pre-arrange publishers, editors and doctoral researchers. Cumulative doctoral paths are clarified as own scenario with supervision and faculty; recognized contributions and archived edition versions receive comprehensible authorship and references.

early front-end development

We start early and iteratively, but do the expansion according to the available material. A technical framework can be prepared from the start of the project. Technical views grow with a representative TEI pilot collection. Thus, the front end remains close to the respective edition stand instead of meeting a supposedly final inventory at the end.

In our case, the front end expansion follows with slight overlap on the actual edition work. This leaves little time for professional feedback before the sponsor. Falk therefore agrees at the beginning of the project an advanced technical preliminary and fixed development window with the chair's own IT. The existing capacity is re-planned; additional financial burdens are avoided. Tasks and time requirements are recorded in the updated work plan.

Start: as early as possible, as late as necessary. Decrease core functions in time; then optimize as long as agreed capacity is available.

Digital views can be closely traced to the current edition state and examined together. The sentence is in our model at the publisher's. Early sentence previews are not prepared ourselves in the project; relevant later typesetting corrections are returned in a controlled manner.
